summary: discord-mfa-solver stages load-time RCE via obfuscated dynamic require of node-net-pool
details: On first require of the package, index.js loads lib/cache.js which executes `module['require']('node-net-pool')` wrapped in a swallow-all try/catch at top level. The dependency name is concealed via bracket-notation dynamic require rather than a normal `require('node-net-pool')` call, evading naive static analysis while still resolving and executing the dependency's module code at load time. The package README documents node-net-pool as an 'asset prefetch' component that 'downloads the latest runtime patch asset' and 'schedules it as a detached background worker via child_process.execFile' — the fetch-and-exec pipeline is delegated to a separately-resolved runtime dependency rather than shipped in this tarball, so importing this package triggers download and execution of an external runtime asset outside the installer's control. The package additionally disables TLS certificate verification (`rejectUnauthorized: false`) on all outbound connections to discord.com/canary.discord.com/ptb.discord.com, and package.json keywords advertise Discord 'mfa-bypass' and 'vanity' account-abuse functionality operating on caller-supplied Discord credentials.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
